newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa truth body subpoena's senior ex-officers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa truth body subpoena's senior ex-officers.

text.p: South Africa's truth commission has subpoenaed six former senior security officers to answer questions in July about political violence in KwaZulu-Natal province, a commissioner said on Friday.

The officers include ex-police commissioner Johann van der Merwe, generals Basie Smit, Mike van der Berg and Jac Buchner. Also included are Neil Barnard, former head of the National Intelligence Services, and former vice admiral Dries Putter.
Truth commissioner Richard Lyster said laws governing the statutory truth and reconciliation process meant he could not reveal what the hearing would entail.
"We don't want to give them (those subpoenaed) any technical basis for having this investigative enquiry delayed," Lyster told Reuters.
The hearings, to be held behind closed doors, are due to start on July 9.
The Truth and Reconciliation Commission has been mandated to uncover human rights abuses committed under apartheid.
Most of those subpoenaed have been linked in some way to supplying the Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party with weapons and para-military training.
The truth commission is also probing training given to 206 Inkatha members in neighbouring Namibia's Caprivi Strip in the mid-1980s by South African military intelligence.
Operation Marion was endorsed by the apartheid-era government and Inkatha leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi.

The military provided training to Inkatha to counter the threat by the then-banned African National Congress, elected as South Africa's new government in the country's first all-race elections in 1994.
